perf.summary: sumArr is int; on accumulation-heavy DSU-on-tree merges int sums can overflow — consider widening or documenting bound.
perf.currentCost: sumArr is int*. Merge accumulates sumArr[aRoot] += sumArr[bRoot] and Update adds val repeatedly. For large n with many merges the running sum can exceed int range, silently wrapping (Burst has no overflow checks).
perf.proposedChange: If counts/sums can exceed 2^31, switch sumArr to long* (as PersistentLazySeg already does). If the design guarantees sums fit in int, document the invariant with a named constant/comment so callers know the safe bound; otherwise widen.
perf.rationale: Prevents silent wraparound corruption on large inputs — a correctness concern, not just perf. Matches the long-based design already used in PersistentLazySeg for the same family of structures.
perf.risk: Widening to long doubles sumArr memory traffic and cache footprint; only do it if overflow is actually reachable for intended n. This is a semantics/correctness flag, not a guaranteed speedup — keep int if the caller contract bounds sums to int range.
